en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to keep newborns warm without electricity.
The sampaguita, our national flower, contains essential oils that possess natural antibacterial properties useful in traditional wound cleaning.
Firecrackers produce sound levels over 120 decibels, which can permanently damage the delicate hair cells inside a child's inner ear.
The Ifugao people cultivate red rice, which contains higher levels of heart-healthy antioxidants and fiber than regular white rice.
The local government unit's disaster risk reduction council uses science-based storm surge maps to evacuate coastal residents before typhoons hit.
National Scientist Dr. Edgardo Gomez studied coral reefs, which act as natural physical barriers that reduce wave energy and prevent coastal erosion.
The Department of Health scientifically validates lagundi, a traditional herbal plant containing active compounds that effectively relieve coughs and asthma.
Wearing a standard motorcycle helmet reduces fatal head injuries by using foam liners to absorb kinetic energy during a traffic crash.
The carabao, our national animal, wallows in mud to cool its body because it lacks enough sweat glands for proper thermoregulation.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo applied the physics of light and shadow to accurately depict bright tropical sunlight in his famous paintings.
Fermenting fish to make bagoonat produces lactic acid, which lowers the food's pH and prevents the growth of harmful spoilage bacteria.
Properly segregating biodegradable waste for composting prevents the anaerobic decomposition in landfills that produces harmful methane greenhouse gases.
